problem: Visual navigation policies are reactive and myopic and collapse to a single mode. Existing world-model pipelines either train the policy and world model separately, or unify them with latent representations that lack explicit geometric/semantic structure and with single-trajectory action outputs.
motivation: Navigation requires anticipating future states, and real-world navigation has multiple feasible trajectories toward a goal. Perception, action and generation share the same spatio-temporal dynamics, so joint training should let them reinforce each other. A diverse action set is also what makes a world model useful as a planner.
key_idea: Jointly train one Bidirectional-Mamba backbone with latent world tokens (depth/semantic-supervised), an anchor-based multimodal trajectory head and a CDiT flow-matching world model, then use the world model's imagined futures to pick the best among the candidate trajectories.
insight: The module ablation shows that world reasoning, action prediction and world modeling reinforce each other: the full model gets ATE 0.254 / PSNR 17.622 versus 0.338 / 14.286 without reasoning. Anchor-based multimodal proposals give the highest trajectory diversity (APD 1.49) and gain far more from world-model planning (ATE 0.85→0.36) than GMM (0.88→0.79) or a diffusion head (0.86→0.58), so proposal diversity is what makes foresight planning work. Gains saturate at about K≈7 candidates.
method: Backbone: the VAE-encoded history, current frame and goal are prepended with learnable latent world tokens and fed to a Bidirectional Mamba (SSM); attentional pooling compresses history tokens into a fixed-length scene representation H.
Latent World Reasoning: world tokens are upsampled by a CNN decoder to predict future depth and semantics, supervised by pseudo-labels from Depth Anything V2 (scale-invariant loss) and SAM (MSE).

Anchor-based multimodal trajectory proposal: K anchors from K-Means + Farthest Point Sampling; an intent head gives anchor probabilities and a control head regresses offsets; an MLP then directly regresses the waypoints for each target. Only the matched anchor is supervised (Huber + NLL).

World model for visual foresight: CDiT blocks conditioned on the predicted actions (converted to optical flow, fused with the timestep via AdaLN) and on H via cross-attention; trained with flow matching, and the VAE decoder produces future frames.
Foresight planning: for each of the K candidate trajectories, imagine the future observations and choose the one best aligned with the goal image, in a closed loop.

Two-stage training: stage 1 jointly trains everything with teacher forcing (100k steps); stage 2 freezes the backbone and heads and fine-tunes the CDiT on predicted trajectories (50k steps) to reduce exposure bias. Kendall uncertainty weighting balances the losses.

setting.backbone: Bidirectional Mamba SSM + CDiT world model + MLP heads, with a pretrained SD VAE (trained jointly)
setting.training_data: Go Stanford, SCAND, RECON and HuRoN robotics datasets; depth/semantic pseudo-labels from Depth Anything V2 and SAM; TartanDrive used as zero-shot test only
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (4 past frames + current) + goal image, 256x256
setting.action_space: predicted relative 2D waypoints + rotation (4-step horizon), multimodal trajectory candidates
setting.simulator: none (offline robotics datasets; rollouts on dataset segments)
setting.privileged: none at test time (depth/semantic pseudo-labels are used only during training)

numbers.extra: World model used as planner; success radius 0.5 m; average segment length 43 steps
numbers.evidence: Table 2 Navigation rollout results, Seen (SR printed as 0.72). Text elsewhere says SR 0.74 in the seen setting, which is inconsistent.

numbers.extra: Zero-shot on unseen environments; world model used as planner; success radius 0.5 m
numbers.evidence: Table 2 Navigation rollout results, Unseen (SR printed as 0.44)

numbers.bench: other:Offline single-step evaluation (avg of four datasets)

numbers_note: Text inconsistencies: it states SR 0.63 for random sampling in seen and SR 0.74 with the planner in seen, while Table 2 prints 0.72; the intro says 66%→72%. The text also mentions ATE 0.164 in the ablation, which the table does not show (0.254). The K-ablation is given only in a figure.
results: NavWM outperforms UniWM on offline metrics (ATE 0.302→0.207, RPE 0.116→0.066, PSNR 14.172→17.340) and on image-goal rollouts (SR 0.66→0.72 seen, 0.36→0.44 unseen on TartanDrive). The strongest baselines are UniWM and NWM.
limitations: Evaluated only offline on recorded robot datasets (no simulator or real-robot deployment), with a short 4-step prediction horizon.
Foresight planning requires generating K candidate futures with a diffusion model, adding inference cost.
The paper is inconsistent about some reported numbers (SR 0.72 vs 0.74; ATE 0.164 vs 0.254), and the unseen success rate is still only 44%.
